messages.content: if i had more time, i would walk to the library. does that say i have more time today?
no. it is about what you would do with more time. it does not tell us that you have that time today.
can you ask me whether i really have time now?
do you have time to walk to the library today?
no. i have to be at work soon. i only want to write about what i would like to do.
then your first sentence works for that idea. it keeps the wish apart from what is possible in your day right now.
what if i say i have more time, so i will walk to the library?
then you are saying the time is there and the walk is your plan. that is different from a wish about more time.
can the library be the same place in both sentences?
yes. the place can stay the same while the information about time and the plan changes.
write one short sentence that keeps the wish but leaves the library out.
if i had more time, i would go for a walk.
does that tell you where i would walk?
no. it only gives the idea of a walk, not the place.
i wait by the door after school, but today i am waiting by the library. are those two sentences about different things?
yes. the first can be about what you usually do after school. the other gives the place where you are waiting today.
so did the place i use on most days have to be wrong?
no. on most days you can wait by the door, while today is different.
write a short message telling my father where to find me today.
i am waiting by the library today, not by the door.
what if he only reads the first part of my first message?
he might think you are by the door if he only reads the first part. the message about today makes the change clear.
should i say i never wait by the door now?
not unless that is what you mean. one day at the library does not make a rule about every day after this.
keep the answer to what you know from my words.
you usually wait by the door after school, but today you are waiting by the library.
what part is the most useful for finding me now?
the place you gave for today: by the library.
which question is right: does he go to school, or does he goes to school?
does he go to school is right.
why is goes not right there?
in that question, use go after does. for a sentence without the question, say he goes to school.
what if i am not asking a question?
you could say: he goes to school.
can you give me the same kind of example with read?
does he read the book? he reads the book.
now make it about they.
do they read the book? they read the book.
so can i just keep does for every person?
no. in these examples, use does with he and do with they.
write only the question about her, using she.
does she read the book?
now answer yes in a full short sentence.
yes, she reads the book.
do you know a real person is reading from that example?
no. these are grammar examples, not facts about a person you have told me about.
should i write i gave they the book or i gave them the book?
i gave them the book is correct.
can they still be right at the start of another sentence?
yes. you could say: they gave me the book.
are those the same people doing the giving?
no. in i gave them the book, you did the giving. in they gave me the book, the other people gave it to you.
what is the same in both examples?
both are about a book moving from one person or group to another. who gives and who gets it changes.
put she and her in examples too.
she gave me the book. i gave her the book.
if i ask who gave it in the first of those, what is the answer?
she did.
now make it a full sentence.
she gave you the book.
why did me change to you in that answer?
because i am answering you about your example. the person who got the book is still you.
in this story, a mother has a son and a daughter. the son goes to visit his grandmother. his sister is at home with their mother. who stayed with the mother?
the daughter stayed with her mother.
can you give me a shorter answer?
the daughter.
who went to visit the grandmother?
the son.
does the story tell us whether the father went too?
no. you have not told me where the father was.
give me the same answer another way.
you have not told me whether the father went or stayed home.
now add one fact: the father was at work. can you say who was at home?
the mother and daughter were at home. the father was at work, and the son was visiting his grandmother.
did adding that fact change where the son was?
no. it gave information about the father. the son still went to see his grandmother.
give me only the place of the father.
at work.
i put a book and a cup on the table. then i moved it to the shelf. where is the cup?
i need to know which object you moved. did it mean the book or the cup?
i mean the book. the cup stayed on the table.
then the cup is on the table, and the book is on the shelf.
what if i now say i broke it?
i would ask again which object you mean. both the cup and book have been part of the conversation, and it alone may not be clear.
can you ask just that question?
which object do you mean?
the cup. now tell me what happened to the book.
you moved the book to the shelf. you did not say you broke the book.
why not make it the broken object too?
because you said the cup was the object you broke. that does not tell us the book broke too.
give me a shorter answer.
you broke the cup, not the book, from what you told me.
i have six coins and my sister has two. i give her one coin. how many do we have now?
you have five coins, and your sister has three.
how many coins do we have together?
eight coins together.
why did the number together stay the same?
you moved one coin between the two of you. you did not add a new coin or take one away from the group.
now my sister finds another coin on the floor. what changes?
if she puts the found coin with hers, she has four, and you still have five. together you have nine.
does finding it mean she can keep it?
not by itself. the count and whose coin it is are different questions.
keep the answer about how many coins for now.
there are nine coins between you and your sister if that found coin is added to the first eight.
say it more simply.
with the found coin added, you have five and she has four. that makes nine together.
what if we put that found coin in another place and keep only our original coins together?
then your original coins are still five for you and three for her.
we have bread and soup ready for dinner. my brother asks if we can make rice too. i want to eat soon.
you can ask whether the rice is important to him today or whether the ready food is enough. that keeps the choice about what both of you need.
he says he just thought rice would be nice, but soup is fine.
then you can keep dinner simple and have the soup and bread. he has said the meal works for him.
should i say he never wants rice?
no. he said soup is fine today. that does not tell us he never wants rice.
write a short thing i could say to him.
let us have the soup and bread today, and think about rice another day.
can you make it less like a rule for tomorrow?
let us have the soup and bread today. we can choose another meal next time.
what did your change leave open?
it left open what you will eat another day. it did not make rice something you have to choose next.
give me a simple last answer.
you can still choose what to eat another day.
if i say the room felt cold, do you know whether i mean the air or how people were with each other?
not always. cold can be about the air, or it can be used to say the people did not seem warm and kind. more detail would help.
i mean i needed a blanket.
then you are talking about the air feeling cold. you can say: the room was cold, so i got a blanket.
what if i mean nobody wanted to speak to me?
then it would help to say that in those words, rather than leave the meaning only in cold. you could say: nobody spoke to me when i came in.
can i say both if both happened?
yes. you can give both facts: the room was cold, and nobody spoke to me when i came in.
does one fact tell us the other must be true?
no. cold air does not tell us that people do not want to talk, and people being quiet does not tell us the air is cold.
give a shorter explanation.
no. the air and the conversation are different parts of the room.
here is a story. a boy went home early because he had left his book there. he took the book and came back to the library. why did he go home?
because he had left his book at home.
was going home the end of the whole visit to the library?
no. he came back to the library after getting the book.
can i say he went home because he did not like the library?
not from the story. the reason given is the book at home.
make a short question whose answer is the library.
where did he go back to after getting the book?
the library. now make the answer early.
when did he go home?
that question could have many answers. ask whether it was early or late.
did he go home early or late?
what did you keep apart when answering why?
i kept the reason about the book apart from a feeling about the library that the story did not give.
just give the reason again.
he went home because he had left his book there.
i like walking in the garden, but i do not know the name of every plant. my cousin says that must mean i do not really like it.
you can enjoy a place without knowing every detail about it. you can like the garden even if you do not know each plant name.
i like the quiet and the way it changes through the year.
those are real things to enjoy. you can also learn about a plant later if you want to, but you do not need every answer before going on the walk.
say it more simply.
you can enjoy the quiet and the changes. if you want to learn about one plant later, you can ask about that one.
write a short reply to my cousin.
i like the garden even though i do not know every plant name. the quiet and the changes through the year are what i enjoy.
can i also say it is never useful to know a plant name?
that would go too far. knowing a name can be useful, even if you do not need it for the kind of visit you enjoy.
give me a simple answer.
you can enjoy the garden and still think learning a plant name may be useful.
change this to they: we walked to the village and put our books on the table.
they walked to the village and put their books on the table.
did our have to become their?
yes, for that meaning. you are now talking about the same people from outside the group, so their keeps the books with those people.
what if i kept our books in the sentence?
then it could mean they put the books of you and your group on the table. that would change whose books they were.
keep the answer simple.
our books could mean the books of you and your group, rather than the books of the people called they.
now say the first sentence using i and one book.
i walked to the village and put my book on the table.
can you put all three examples together?
we put our books on the table. they put their books on the table. i put my book on the table.
who has one book in the last example?
the person saying i has one book.
i want to write about my whole family, but i do not know where to begin.
what do you want the writing to be for: a school task, a letter, or a story just for yourself?
it is a school task. the teacher asked for one page, not a whole book.
then choose a small part of family life for that page. one visit, one meal, or a person helping you could give it a clear idea to follow.
give me a question to choose that part.
what is one family moment you remember clearly?
my grandfather showed me an old photo and told me who was in it.
that sounds like enough for a first story. you can begin with where you were, then tell what he showed you and what you learned.
write the first sentence without adding a place i did not give.
my grandfather showed me an old photo and told me about the people in it.
what question do you need to know the place?
where were you when he showed you the photo?
in his kitchen.
then you could begin: in his kitchen, my grandfather showed me an old photo.
i made a plan to read this morning, but my cousin came to visit and i did not read. should i stop making plans?
one changed morning does not mean every plan is wrong. you can look at what changed and choose what to do with the reading later.
i did enjoy the visit.
then the morning had something good in it, even though it did not go like your first plan. you could choose another time to read if you still want to.
what if i am not free again today?
then the reading may have to wait until another day. that does not tell us the whole idea of a plan is wrong.
give me a short sentence to remember.
a plan can change when the day changes.
does that mean i should never keep a plan?
no. a plan can help, and you can also change it when something new is important. both are possible.
give me an example using my morning.
you wanted to read, then chose time with your cousin. you can make a new reading plan for another day.
what fact should you not forget about the visit?
you said you enjoyed it.
write a story about a girl holding a book for a friend for a short time before giving it back. use a garment in the story too.

a girl and her friend were leaving the library. the friend needed to put on a warm garment and asked the girl to hold her book. the girl held it while waiting by the door. when her friend was ready, she gave the book back. they then walked to the park together. the girl had held the book for a moment, but it was still her friend who had brought it and would take it home.
tell me that last part more simply.
the girl gave the book back because she had only been holding it for her friend.
say whose book it was in a clear sentence.
it was the book her friend had brought. the girl only held it for a moment.
who asked for help?
the friend who needed to put on the garment.
did the girl give her own book away?
no. she gave back the same book she had been holding for her friend.
write only the last two things they did, in order.
she gave the book back, and they walked to the park.
my friend said she went to the park. can i ask what she liked most about the visit?
you can, but that question sounds as if you already know she liked part of it. if you do not know that, you could ask what the visit was like first.
write the open question.
what was your visit to the park like?
she says it was too busy and she came home early.
then a question about what she liked most might not be the best next question. you could ask what made it feel too busy or whether she wants to talk about it.
what if i just want to be kind and not ask many things?
you could say: i hope you have some quiet time now that you are home.
can you write a reply that leaves it up to her whether to talk about the visit?
yes. you could say: would you like to talk about the visit?
give me a message that starts with the information she gave me.
you said it was too busy and you came home early. i am here if you want to talk about it.
now give me just a short question that does not add a feeling.
would you like to talk about the visit?
put these things in order for a story, not as a whole cooking plan: the soup is given to people, the vegetables are cut, and the vegetables go in the pot.
first the vegetables are cut, then they go in the pot, and later the soup is given to people.
give me the same order again using simple words.
first the vegetables are cut, then they go in the pot, and later the soup is given to the people who will eat it.
does that tell me everything about making soup?
no. it only puts the three parts you gave in order. it is not every detail of making real soup.
keep the explanation simple.
no. those are only the three parts you gave. there could be more to do in a whole cooking plan.
can you just say it is not a whole plan?
yes. it is an order for those three parts, not a whole plan for cooking soup.
why should you not add a cooking time when i only asked for the order?
because that would add information you did not give and did not ask for.
give the order once more.
cut the vegetables, put them in the pot, and later give the soup to the people.
i heard a short sound behind the door, but i did not see what made it. can i say a book made it?
not for sure. the sound by itself does not tell us what object made it.
keep the answer simple.
you heard a short sound behind the door. you did not see what made it.
what if i later open the door and see a book on the floor?
that gives more information, but it still may not tell you how the sound happened. you can say what you heard and what you saw.
write one sentence with both facts.
i heard a short sound behind the door and later saw a book on the floor.
can i say someone chose to put the book on the floor?
not from those facts. you have not said you saw a person move the book.
give me a short answer about what i do not know.
you do not know whether anyone moved the book or whether a person made the sound.
why is it useful to keep those parts open?
it keeps the answer about what you know rather than adding a story as a fact.
my book is either on the shelf or in the bedroom. which is it?
i cannot choose from that alone. you gave two possible places, but no fact that makes one the answer.
what should i check first?
you could choose the place that is easiest to look at. where did you last see the book?
on the shelf yesterday. i have not checked today.
then the shelf is a useful first place to check, but yesterday does not tell us it is still there now.
say that more simply.
look on the shelf first because you last saw it there. you still need to check whether it is there now.
if it is not on the shelf, must it be in the bedroom?
only if those really are the only two possible places. if other places are possible too, then we do not know yet.
give a simple answer.
if those are the only two places it can be, then not on the shelf leaves the bedroom. if other places are possible, we do not know yet.
what did the first either sentence not tell you?
it did not give a reason to choose one place over the other.
i understood one hard page today, and i feel good about it. i still do not understand the next page.
you can be happy about the page you understood without saying the whole book is easy now. one part learned is still part of your goal.
give me a simple reply.
you learned something today. the next hard page does not take that away.
my friend says i should not feel good until i finish the whole book.
you can want to finish the book and still be happy about learning one page. finishing the whole book is not the only part you can enjoy.
say it another way.
you can want to finish the book and also be happy about understanding one page now.
what should i do before starting the next page?
you could say the meaning of the page in your own words, then look at whether the next page builds on that idea.
give me only one small step.
say the meaning of the page you understood in your own words.
just end with something kind, not another task.
you can enjoy what you learned today.
